name: Magma
what_it_is: Magma is an open-source mobile core network platform (BSD-3-Clause, Linux Foundation) that provides an evolved packet core (EPC), cloud orchestrator, and federation gateway supporting 2G/3G/4G and 5G networks over cellular and Wi-Fi access networks. It is designed to allow operators to deploy and manage mobile core infrastructure without vendor lock-in using unmodified commercial radio hardware.
components: Access Gateway (AGW) — implements EPC, AAA, PGW for LTE; interfaces with unmodified eNodeBs
Orchestrator (orc8r) — cloud service for secure configuration, monitoring, and analytics
Federation Gateway (FeG) — proxy integrating Magma AGW with existing MNO core via 3GPP interfaces
NMS — web UI for network management and traffic analytics
magmad — gateway daemon managing all AGW services
sctpd — SCTP transport handler for S1AP/NGAP
oai_mme — MME (Mobility Management Entity) from OpenAirInterface
sessiond — session management and policy enforcement
mobilityd — IP address allocation and mobility management
enodebd — eNodeB configuration and management daemon
measurement: User traffic flows visible in NMS web UI
Analytics dashboards for wireless users via Orchestrator
Event and call trace logs (ctraced, eventd)
configuration: MAGMA_PRINT_GRPC_PAYLOAD environment variable (enables gRPC payload logging)
Configuration templates mounted into services at runtime
Orchestrator hosted on public or private cloud
modes: LTE (4G) EPC mode — AGW implements full evolved packet core
Federation mode — AGW proxied via FeG to existing MNO infrastructure
Carrier Wi-Fi (CWF) mode — AGW with Wi-Fi access network
Dev mode — MAGMA_DEV_MODE flag enables development/debug behavior
constraints: Host system requires a patched Open vSwitch installation for containerized AGW deployment
Linux kernel 5.4+ required for AGW dataplane features
SCTP kernel module support required on host for S1AP/NGAP
Orchestrator requires Kubernetes cluster and Helm charts for cloud deployment
Orchestrator requires PostgreSQL and Redis as backing stores
AGW is Linux-only; no Windows or macOS support
Materials are provided as-is — operators must independently verify security and performance requirements before production use (stated explicitly in README)
notable_absences: No built-in RAN (Radio Access Network) — requires external unmodified commercial eNodeBs/gNodeBs
No built-in IMS/VoLTE core — voice services not documented as included
No HSS (Home Subscriber Server) included in AGW — relies on FeG for MNO HSS integration or local subscriberdb
No PCRF included — policy handled internally via policydb/sessiond, not a standalone 3GPP PCRF
No built-in charging system (OCS/OFCS) — charging delegated to MNO core via FeG
